subtopic: Reaching a fitness or sports goal
subtype: Approach: progressive plan with rest days [Action]
passage: PE teacher's note, Friday. Gopika brought her running diary to show me. She does a run-and-walk session on Monday, Wednesday and Friday, with rest days between, and writes each one down: how far, how it felt, how her legs were the next day. In week four she told me she wanted to add two extra kilometres in one go, because she felt strong. I asked what her legs had said in the diary. She looked again and said, “A bit tight after Wednesday.” She kept to the plan and added only a little more distance. I told her that if a pain keeps going or worries her, she should tell me and see a doctor. I'll read the diary again next Friday. — Suraj

qa.q: How many days a week does Gopika run and walk?
qa.a: Three days a week, with rest days between.

qa.q: How might Gopika have felt when she wanted to add two extra kilometres?
qa.a: Eager and impatient because she felt strong, but she still held to the plan after reading her diary.

qa.q: What should Gopika do if a pain keeps going, and why?
qa.a: Tell the PE teacher and see a doctor, since pain that keeps going or worries her should be checked rather than pushed through.

qa.q: How does the diary look to Suraj?
qa.a: Suraj sees a written record, which makes it easier to notice early if the distance rises too fast.

grounding: A student follows a run-and-walk schedule with rest days, records each session and increases distance slowly.

passage:
Friday, week 5
Session 3 of the week. Run 3 min, walk 1 min, eight times. Legs fine. Breathing okay after the fourth round.
Rest days are still annoying. On Tuesday and Thursday I wanted to go again, but the plan says Monday, Wednesday and Friday only, with a day off between, and Disha (who runs for the district) says rest is when the legs get stronger, not weaker. So I did stretches and homework instead.
Looking back at weeks 1 to 4 in this diary: week 1 was run 1 min, walk 2. My shins hurt a bit in week 2 when I tried to add two things at once, so since then I change only one thing each week: either a longer run or one more round.
Next week: run 4 min, walk 1 min, still eight rounds. No more than that.
– Hemant

qa.q: Which days does Hemant's plan allow for running?
qa.a: Monday, Wednesday and Friday only, with a day off between.

qa.q: How did Hemant feel about the rest days?
qa.a: Hemant found them annoying and felt restless on Tuesday and Thursday, but trusted the plan and Disha's advice.

qa.q: What else could Hemant do if the shin pain comes back?
qa.a: Stay at the same level for a week, and ask a coach or the doctor if the pain keeps going or worries Hemant.

qa.q: How might Disha see Hemant's diary?
qa.a: Disha would likely be pleased to see slow, single changes and rest days respected, the way experienced runners train.

grounding: Shows a student following a three-day run-walk schedule with rest days, recording each session in a diary, and increasing slowly to avoid pain.

Zeenat: and on rest days?

qa.q: What else could Sudha track in the log besides times?
